scope: First-party public sources that can expand application-trend monitoring beyond PubMed. These sources indicate regulatory activity, funded work, methods, trials, procurement, approvals, monitoring programs, or patents; none is treated as proof of market share or customer demand by itself.

sources.name: Crossref REST API
sources.description: Searchable metadata for journal articles, conference proceedings, books, datasets, grants, funders, and publication updates across disciplines.
sources.whatToMeasure: New works, proceedings, grants, funders, and topic growth by market-specific LC, chromatography, and mass-spectrometry query.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds chemistry, food, environmental, engineering, and conference records that may not be indexed in PubMed.

sources.name: OpenAlex API
sources.description: Open catalog connecting scholarly works with topics, institutions, authors, funders, and sources.
sources.whatToMeasure: Topic growth, funded institutions, geographic concentration, and new analytical-workflow clusters.
sources.whyItMatters: Provides institution and funder context that a publication count alone does not show.

sources.name: PATENTSCOPE
sources.description: International and national patent collections searchable by keyword, classification, applicant, and chemical structure.
sources.whatToMeasure: New filings involving LC, LC-MS, sample preparation, automation, assays, and application-specific analytical workflows.
sources.whyItMatters: Surfaces pre-commercial technical direction before it appears in product launches or application notes.

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API
sources.signalCategory: Active development programs and biomarker work
sources.description: Structured study records covering interventions, sponsors, collaborators, outcomes, locations, and study status.
sources.whatToMeasure: New or expanding trials that mention biomarkers, bioanalysis, pharmacokinetics, metabolomics, proteomics, or LC-MS endpoints.
sources.whyItMatters: Shows where analytical demand is entering active development programs rather than only the literature.

sources.name: FDA Drug Approvals and Databases
sources.signalCategory: Approvals, dissolution methods, and product guidance
sources.description: FDA entry point for Drugs@FDA, dissolution methods, product-specific guidance, Orange Book, safety, and approval datasets.
sources.whatToMeasure: New approvals, dosage forms, dissolution methods, impurity requirements, and product-specific analytical guidance.
sources.whyItMatters: Connects pharmaceutical application trends to regulated methods and product pipelines.

sources.name: ICH Q14 Analytical Procedure Development
sources.description: Current regulatory principles for science- and risk-based analytical procedure development and lifecycle management.
sources.whatToMeasure: New expectations affecting method development, validation, transfer, multivariate procedures, and change management.
sources.whyItMatters: Translates regulatory change into LC method-development and software workflow requirements.

sources.name: EMA Quality Guidelines
sources.description: European quality guidance covering active substances, finished products, biologics, specifications, and manufacturing controls.
sources.whatToMeasure: New and revised quality guidelines with implications for chromatography, impurity profiling, validation, and method transfer.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds non-U.S. regulatory demand that may change application priorities for global customers.

sources.name: FDA Purple Book
sources.description: Searchable database of FDA-licensed biological products, reference products, biosimilars, and interchangeable products.
sources.whatToMeasure: New biologic and biosimilar approvals by molecule class, sponsor, and approval history.
sources.whyItMatters: Directly indicates where characterization, comparability, and release-testing workflows may expand.

sources.name: FDA NME and New Biologic Approvals
sources.description: Downloadable compilation of CDER new molecular entity drug and new biologic approvals.
sources.whatToMeasure: Approval counts and modality shifts that create new characterization, impurity, and bioanalytical workloads.
sources.whyItMatters: Provides a regulated pipeline outcome rather than a publication proxy.

sources.name: EMA Medicines Database
sources.description: European public assessment reports and medicine records with indications, approval status, and regulatory history.
sources.whatToMeasure: New approvals, biosimilars, advanced therapies, withdrawals, and assessment themes requiring analytical proof.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds European modality and regulatory signals to U.S.-centric approval data.

sources.name: FDA Drug Establishments Current Registration Site
sources.description: Daily publication of currently registered establishments that manufacture, prepare, compound, or process drugs for the U.S. market.
sources.whatToMeasure: New and changing sites, business operations, geography, and manufacturing footprint by organization.
sources.whyItMatters: Provides a measurable view of the regulated manufacturing base that CDMO application demand serves.

sources.name: FDA Drug Master File List
sources.signalCategory: API, excipient, packaging, and process activity
sources.description: Quarterly list of drug master files with holder, subject, type, and activity status.
sources.whatToMeasure: New active DMFs, holder growth, modality keywords, and geographic concentration.
sources.whyItMatters: Shows where outsourced development and manufacturing complexity is accumulating.

sources.name: FDA Drug Shortages
sources.description: Current and resolved drug-shortage information maintained by FDA.
sources.whatToMeasure: Shortages by dosage form, manufacturer, reason, and duration that may trigger capacity, method-transfer, or release-testing demand.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds operational pressure signals that approval and publication databases do not capture.

sources.name: FDA 510(k) Database
sources.description: Weekly searchable and downloadable premarket-notification records with device name, applicant, product code, decision date, and summaries.
sources.whatToMeasure: New clearances for assays, mass-spectrometry devices, sample preparation, software, and laboratory automation.
sources.whyItMatters: Indicates which clinical workflows are moving into regulated commercial use.

sources.name: CDC NHANES Laboratory Data and Methods
sources.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.description: Laboratory datasets, method documents, and procedures for blood, urine, and other specimen measurements in the U.S. population.
sources.whatToMeasure: New analytes, matrices, LC-MS/MS procedures, instrument requirements, and released population datasets.
sources.whyItMatters: Connects clinical and public-health priorities to exact laboratory methods and matrices.

sources.name: FDA Medical Device Databases
sources.signalCategory: Device approvals, listings, recalls, and adverse events
sources.description: Directory of FDA device datasets including 510(k), PMA, De Novo, registration, listings, recalls, and adverse-event records.
sources.whatToMeasure: Approvals, new entrants, product codes, recalls, and post-market issues for analytical and diagnostic workflows.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds commercial and post-market context around clinical application adoption.

sources.name: NIH RePORTER API
sources.description: Programmatic access to funded projects, abstracts, organizations, investigators, awards, and publications from NIH and partner agencies.
sources.whatToMeasure: New awards and funding totals for LC-MS, chromatography, omics, biomarkers, core facilities, and method development.
sources.whyItMatters: Funding precedes publications and instrument purchases, making it an earlier demand indicator.

sources.name: NSF Award Search
sources.description: Searchable and exportable database of NSF-funded projects since 1989.
sources.whatToMeasure: New awards for analytical instrumentation, chemistry, environmental measurement, automation, and data science.
sources.whyItMatters: Captures non-biomedical research and instrumentation funding missed by PubMed and NIH-only monitoring.

sources.name: CORDIS Projects and Results
sources.description: European Commission repository of funded project factsheets, participants, reports, deliverables, and open-data downloads.
sources.whatToMeasure: New projects, funding, participants, deliverables, and thematic clusters involving analytical workflows.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds European funding and consortium activity that U.S. databases miss.

sources.name: SAM.gov Contracting
sources.description: Central U.S. source for contract opportunities, award records, subcontract reports, and contracting-data downloads.
sources.whatToMeasure: Open and awarded opportunities for LC, chromatography, mass spectrometry, laboratory automation, service, and consumables.
sources.whyItMatters: Shows explicit government buying activity rather than scientific interest alone.

sources.name: USAspending.gov Data
sources.description: Official federal award data with agency, recipient, award type, geography, and spending details.
sources.whatToMeasure: Award values and recipients for analytical instruments, lab services, maintenance, consumables, and research programs.
sources.whyItMatters: Confirms where government budgets are actually being awarded after opportunities are posted.

sources.name: Grants.gov Search
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.description: Central search for U.S. federal grant opportunities across agencies.
sources.whatToMeasure: New funding calls requiring laboratory measurement, public-health testing, environmental analysis, food safety, or scientific infrastructure.
sources.whyItMatters: Identifies application demand before projects are awarded and published.

sources.name: Tenders Electronic Daily
sources.description: Official EU public-procurement portal for tender notices and contract awards.
sources.whatToMeasure: New and awarded tenders for chromatography, mass spectrometry, laboratory systems, service, and application-specific testing.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds non-U.S. public buying activity and named laboratory requirements.

sources.name: EPA UCMR 5 Data
sources.description: National occurrence data, analytical methods, minimum reporting levels, and monitoring design for 29 PFAS and lithium.
sources.whatToMeasure: Reported occurrence, participating systems, analyte prevalence, method coverage, reporting limits, and new data releases.
sources.whyItMatters: Links PFAS application demand to national testing volume, matrices, methods, and reporting limits.

sources.name: EPA SW-846 Compendium
sources.description: More than 200 sampling and analytical methods, including chromatographic, HPLC, MS, and LC-MS/MS methods such as PFAS Method 8327.
sources.whatToMeasure: New, revised, and validated methods; analytes; matrices; extraction procedures; and instrument techniques.
sources.whyItMatters: Turns regulatory method changes into concrete application, sample-preparation, and performance requirements.

sources.name: EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard
sources.description: EPA platform integrating chemistry, toxicity, exposure, bioactivity, and monitoring information for environmental chemicals.
sources.whatToMeasure: Chemicals gaining data coverage, monitoring lists, exposure evidence, and analytical-method needs.
sources.whyItMatters: Helps identify emerging analytes before they become standardized testing markets.

sources.name: USDA Pesticide Data Program
sources.signalCategory: Food pesticide residues and laboratory methods
sources.description: Program data, annual reports, analytical methods, commodity testing history, quality-control procedures, and laboratory SOPs.
sources.whatToMeasure: Commodities tested, analytes, LC-MS/MS methods, reporting limits, detections, and method revisions.
sources.whyItMatters: Connects food-safety trends to actual matrices, residue panels, and laboratory procedures.

sources.name: FDA Pesticide Analytical Manual
sources.description: Official manual covering regulatory operations, multiresidue methods, HPLC, recoveries, and pesticide analytical procedures.
sources.whatToMeasure: New or revised residue methods, analytes, matrices, recoveries, cleanup steps, and LC requirements.
sources.whyItMatters: Provides exact enforcement-method needs rather than general food-science publication counts.

sources.name: FDA Bacteriological Analytical Manual
sources.description: FDA laboratory procedures for microbiological analysis of foods, beverages, and cosmetics.
sources.whatToMeasure: New and revised chapters, organism targets, matrices, toxins, confirmation methods, and sample-preparation needs.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds regulated pathogen and toxin testing demand outside the chemical-residue literature.

sources.name: EU Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed
sources.description: European rapid-alert information on food and feed safety notifications, hazards, products, and countries.
sources.whatToMeasure: Rising hazard categories, matrices, contaminants, countries, and repeated notification patterns that imply testing demand.
sources.whyItMatters: Adds current hazard and enforcement signals that can precede new routine testing workflows.
